title: First Interview
description:
A company {name} applied to gets back to him. Mapo-gu. Third floor. No elevator.

The sign reads 'Mirae Industrial Tech.' Its website has no information. He searches. Two blogs. Both stopped updating two years ago.

The interviewer is in her early forties. She picks up the résumé, adjusts her glasses, and reads it slowly.
The air conditioner hums. A motorcycle passes outside. Silence, waiting for something.

"There's a six-year gap here."

Those six years. His father's loan guarantee. The other party disappeared. {name} paid what remained.
He cannot turn those six years into one sentence.

{name} looks away and takes the last flight.

Fine. So what if I'm odd.

title: The Number
description:
Goshiwon room. 3 AM. {name} couldn't sleep.

Opened the calculator on the phone.

Minimum wage. Not even 2 million won for a full month of work.
Three billion won ÷ 2 million won = 1,500 months = 125 years.

125 years.

{name} stared at the screen. Laughed, because it was absurd.
Salary alone — mathematically impossible. From the beginning.

Then the phone rang.
Father. At 3 AM.

{name} didn't pick up. Not while staring at this number — there was no way to keep his voice steady.

choices.text: Keep searching job apps after the shift. Seed money first. [Saver mindset]
choices.result_text:
Big money starts from small money.
Even after work, {name} kept scanning job apps. Side work, temp work, two jobs.

Seed money. That's the first gate.
The number 125 years kept drifting in front of the eyes.

choices.text: Go to the library after work. Start studying investing. [Investor mindset]
choices.result_text:
YouTube, books, finance forums.
After work, {name} went to the library.

If salary won't work, money has to work instead.
Compound interest. Leverage. Assets. {name} read those words seriously for the first time.

choices.text: Write business ideas in the notebook. [Founder mindset]
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote something in a notebook.
Gaps. Demand. Supply. What nobody else was doing.

Ideas alone are nothing yet.
But people who write nothing down never begin.

description_orthodox:
Goshiwon. 3 AM.

Couldn't sleep. Opened the calculator on the phone.

Wage 10,000 won/hour. Two million won a month. Gangnam, 3 billion won. 125 years.

{name} wrote down more numbers. Save 3 million won a month. 15% annual return. Compounding.
What looks impossible to the gut, broken into numbers, starts to show a path.
Then the phone rang. Father. At 3 AM.

He didn't pick up. The clearer the path got, the less he knew where to even begin.
description_unorthodox:
Goshiwon. 3 AM.

Couldn't sleep. Opened the calculator on the phone.

Wage 10,000 won/hour. 125 years.

{name} shut the calculator off. This way won't work.
He'd known that from the start. So he needed another way — a different axis than time.
He had to see what others didn't.

Then the phone rang. Father. At 3 AM.

He didn't pick up. The more set he was on finding another road, the heavier that voice felt.
description_low_mental:
Goshiwon. 3 AM.

Couldn't sleep again.

Opened the calculator, then closed it. The number — 125 years — stayed in front of his eyes. Even doing nothing.

His body felt heavy. The air in this room felt heavy.

The phone rang. Father. {name} thought for a moment about whether to answer.

title: 2 AM
description:
2 AM. The goshiwon room.

Staring at the ceiling, {name}'s hand reaches for the phone. Instagram.

Park Minho — 'Finally, my own place 🏠 Won an LH housing lottery T_T Waited 10 years'
Lee Suhyeon — Maldives honeymoon. Pale blue sea. A wedding dress.
Kim Junghoon — BMW 3 Series key.

Everyone has arrived somewhere.

{name} looks at the stain on the goshiwon wall. A mark left by damp. He does not know how long it has been there.
Rent: 650,000 won. Another calendar page is turning in this room.

choices.text: Delete the app — comparison is poison.
choices.result_text:
He holds the icon down. The small X trembles, then vanishes.

The black screen holds only the fluorescent light and {name}'s face.
His finger taps the empty space once more out of habit.

choices.text: Use that feeling as fuel — just you wait.
choices.result_text:
Envy burns at the back of {name}'s throat.

He opens Notes and writes three things to do tomorrow. The battery reaches nine percent as he types the last period.
When he turns the phone facedown, the pipe behind the wall sounds louder.

choices.text: Just look. Jealous is jealous.
choices.result_text: He scrolls to the end and even taps Like. After the count rises by one, {name} still cannot turn off the screen.

description_orthodox:
2 AM. The goshiwon room.

{name} opens Instagram and stops mid-scroll.

The corner of Minho's housing contract. Maldives sand on Suhyeon's ankle. A BMW key resting in Junghoon's palm.

The minute display in the corner changes once. His thumb cannot move to the next photo.

{name} looks between the damp wallpaper and the new living room on the screen.
description_unorthodox:
2 AM. The goshiwon room.

{name} opens Instagram. Other people's lives slide past like ads.

A bank-loan envelope is cropped out at the edge of the housing contract. The slide after the Maldives beach shows an airport baggage line. Black grease remains under the thumbnail holding the BMW key.

{name} pinches the photos twice, trying to see beyond their frames.

Someone snores next door. Only the Like counts move, one at a time.
description_long_gosiwon:
2 AM.

{name} opens Instagram again. Seventh month in this room.

Park Minho, housing-lottery win. Lee Suhyeon, newlywed. Kim Junghoon, foreign car.

{name} sets the phone down. In place of the screen, only the damp wallpaper remains in view.

650,000 won rent. Another calendar page is turning in this room. Between the people on the screen and {name}, there is now one more line, and it cannot be seen.

title: Next Door
description:
Hallway outside the goshiwon shared kitchen. 1 AM.

A narrow corridor with only one fluorescent tube working. {name} is carrying cup ramyeon back to the room when the door next to his opens.

The neighbor from next door. They have crossed paths before, but this is their first greeting.
"...You're having ramyeon too, hyung?"

There are dark hollows under his eyes. A worn Grade 9 civil-service exam book is tucked under his arm.

The man brushes a palm over its cover. "I'm Kang Hyunsu, from the room next door. We should've said hello sooner. I've been studying for the civil-service exam for four years."
{name} gives his name too. Hyunsu asks, "What do you do?"

choices.text: 'I don't really know yet. I'm still figuring it out.'
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu nods.
'That's the most honest answer.'

The two of them eat ramyeon in silence in the narrow hallway.

choices.text: 'I'm going to make it to Gangnam within five years.'
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu stops mid-ramyeon and looks at {name}.
{name} expects a laugh. None comes.
'...You mean it, don't you, hyung.'

After a short silence, Hyunsu speaks quietly.
'I don't know why, but I think you'll actually make it.'

description_orthodox:
Hallway outside the goshiwon shared kitchen. 1 AM.

As {name} turns to head back with his cup ramyeon, the man next door comes out.

"You're having ramyeon too, hyung?"

A Grade 9 civil-service exam book. Worn cover. A book held for a long time.

"I'm Kang Hyunsu, from the room next door. We should've said hello sooner. I've been studying for the civil-service exam for four years." {name} gives his name too. Hyunsu asks, "What do you do?"

This path is a path too. The sure, slow one.
{name} briefly measures the road he has chosen against Hyunsu's.
description_unorthodox:
Hallway outside the goshiwon shared kitchen. 1 AM.

The man next door comes out.

"You're having ramyeon too, hyung?"

A worn Grade 9 civil-service exam book is tucked under his arm.

"I'm Kang Hyunsu, from the room next door. We should've said hello sooner. I've been studying for the civil-service exam for four years." {name} gives his name too. Hyunsu asks, "What do you do?"

{name} wonders what Hyunsu sees, studying that every single day.
If he passes, where does he go? On 2.2 million won a month, can he even get out of this goshiwon?
He does not ask. Everyone has their own math.

title: Two Months In
description:
2 AM.

The ramyeon broth had gone cold.
After Hyunsu went back inside, {name} stood in the hallway alone for a while.

His first two months in Seoul — the burner account text, his father's call, the first Gangnam cafe he ever walked into, Hyunsu's ramyeon.

{name} returned to the room where he currently lived and opened the notebook. First line:
'{notebook_motive}'

Below it: '3 billion won. Five years.' The pages after that were still empty.

Under fluorescent light: a small room. One desk. One blanket.
Can 3 billion won actually come out of here?

{name} still didn't have an answer.
But tonight was the first time the question felt completely real.

choices.text: Close the notebook. That's enough for today.
choices.result_text:
Turned off the light.

In the dark, the number 3 billion won remained.
The distance between that number and this room — that's exactly the distance ahead.

{name} closed his eyes. No plan yet. Still — he thought he could sleep tonight.

choices.text: Write one more line: 'Wake up at 7 AM tomorrow.'
choices.result_text:
Below the two sentences, {name} wrote: '7 AM tomorrow.'

Three billion won is far. 7 AM is close.
He decided to start with the smallest thing he could actually do right now.

He turned off the light. Tomorrow might be just a little different from today.

title: Why Gangnam?
description:
Late March, just after the rain. A real estate office in a Sinchon alley displayed rows of studio floor plans behind its glass door.

{name} had come to see whether leaving the goshiwon was even possible.
"Ten million won down. 550,000 a month. Utilities extra."
The numbers on the calculator were far ahead of the money in the bank.

The man across the desk looked from {name}'s empty hands to the worn sneakers. Early fifties, with a restrained Chungcheong cadence.
"With your situation right now, this will be difficult."

{name} pushed back the chair. Without looking up from the paperwork, the man spoke again.
"Wait. No reason to throw the person out just because the room is out of reach."

He took out two paper cups.
"I can offer you hot coffee. The rain just stopped."

Only the wall clock and tires pushing through wet pavement filled the office.

choices.text: "How did you know my situation?"
choices.result_text:
The man finally looked up from the papers.

"Was I wrong?"

{name} said nothing. The man nodded toward the empty chair. His gaze felt less like kindness now and more like confirmation.

choices.text: "I'll just have the coffee, then."
choices.result_text:
The paper cup was hot enough to sting, and the instant coffee was far too sweet.

When {name} sat again, the man pulled out the opposite chair. Why he would spend time on someone who could not afford a room remained unclear.

description_orthodox:
Late March, just after the rain. A real estate office in a Sinchon alley displayed rows of studio floor plans behind its glass door.

Ten million won down, 550,000 a month, plus utilities. The numbers still refused to work with the current income.

The man across the desk watched the order of {name}'s calculations.
"With your situation right now, this will be difficult."

What had given it away? Or did everyone who came looking for a room wear the same face?

When {name} stood, the man took out two paper cups.
"I can offer you hot coffee. The rain just stopped."

First, determine whether this was someone to learn from or someone to guard against.
description_unorthodox:
Late March, just after the rain. Rows of studio floor plans hung behind wet glass in a Sinchon alley.

Ten million won down. 550,000 a month. Still too far.

"With your situation right now, this will be difficult." The man across the desk had read {name} before reading the calculator.

Eyes that priced people. In front of eyes like that, it was hard to tell whether standing first meant losing or staying seated did.

The man took out two paper cups.
"I can offer you hot coffee. The rain just stopped."

{name} looked once more at the eyes, not the cup.

title: The Measure of a Person
description:
The man turns the calculator toward {name}. The nameplate on the desk reads Im Sangchul.

"You asked about the deposit first. You checked the utilities twice. You looked at the rent before the windows."

"And that tells you everything?"

"People with money ask which way to go. People trying to survive ask where the exits are."
Sangchul taps the cold numbers once with his fingertip.

{name} draws the worn toes of his sneakers back beneath the chair.
"Do you measure everyone like that?"

"No. That's why I offered coffee."

It is an odd amount of certainty from a stranger. Sangchul does not press for an answer. He waits until the steam above the paper cup has nearly disappeared.

choices.text: "Then how far do you think I can go?"
choices.result_text:
Sangchul's faint smile vanishes.

"That isn't mine to decide."

He slides a blank memo sheet to the center. This time his eyes are not measuring. They are waiting.

title: One Paper Cup
description:
Sangchul moves the stack of contracts aside. Somehow the desk looks wider when he serves coffee than when he shows rooms.

"Everyone who comes to Seoul looking for a room starts with numbers. How much to move in. How much to earn to survive."

"Those aren't the wrong questions."

"No. But people who enter with nothing but numbers are usually the first to leave because of them."

A car splits the wet road beyond the glass. Sangchul waits until the sound passes before continuing.

"You ask everyone looking for a room why they want to endure Seoul?"

"I do. If all I do is unlock doors, I'm just the man with the keys."

It is impossible to tell whether this is kindness or a sales pitch. But Sangchul has not brought out a single listing. He is waiting for {name}'s answer instead.

choices.text: "That one I can answer."
choices.result_text:
Sangchul slides a blank memo sheet to the center. No price. No address.

"Good. Then we can talk about rooms afterward."

For the first time, the broker's cadence leaves his voice.

title: The Question
description:
Sangchul balances a pen on the blank memo sheet.

"Where do you want to live?"

"...Gangnam."

No laugh. No admiration. Only the long hiss of tires over wet pavement beyond the glass.

"Gangnam isn't one neighborhood. An apartment? An address? Something to show people?"

{name} opens his mouth, then closes it. Every answer that comes to mind sounds borrowed from someone else.

Sangchul sets down the pen.
"That's why I'm asking. Why?"

choices.text: 'I... want to show my father. Just once.'
choices.result_text:
For the first time, that reason is spoken out loud.
"Where are you from?" Sangchul asks.
"Changwon."
The hand stirring his coffee stops — just for half a beat.
Then he looks at {name} for a long moment and nods.
"That 'why' is solid. Then that's enough."
"When you're shaken, it'll hold you." Sangchul sets his business card on the memo sheet.

choices.text: 'Doesn't everyone want Gangnam if they have the money?'
choices.result_text:
Im Sangchul chuckles.
'I've never seen anyone who answers like that actually make it.'
'If Gangnam is the goal, you won't make it. The ones who do see it as a means to an end.'
{name} does not know yet what that means. He leaves with just the business card.

choices.text: Honest — 'Because I refuse to lose. To this city.'
choices.result_text:
Im Sangchul sets down his coffee.
'...I said the same thing thirty years ago, when I came up from Chungcheong.'
'That stubbornness got me this far. Two buildings. But I also lost a lot.'
'Don't lose what matters on the way. If you're going, get there whole.'

title: Contact
description:
At dusk in spring rain, on a back road in Sinchon. {name} is riding a secondhand bicycle to save on transit fares.

A black sedan swings around the corner and clips the front wheel. {name} falls onto the rain-slick road.

A woman who looks to be in her early thirties steps out. Her long black hair and tailored suit are getting soaked.

"Oh no—are you okay? I'm so sorry. You should see a doctor—"

{name} checks the bicycle. The front wheel is bent, and his knee is bleeding a little.
There are still things to finish before the day is over. He cannot afford to spend much longer in the road.

choices.text: 'I'm fine.' — Just leave.
choices.result_text:
Without compensation or contact information, {name} wheels the bent bicycle away.
He does not look back.

The woman remains where she is and watches him disappear down the road.

choices.text: Show the bent wheel — 'Just the repair cost, please.'
choices.result_text:
She takes one 50,000 won note and three 10,000 won notes from her wallet without hesitation.
'Is that enough? If not—'
'It's fine.'

{name} pockets the 80,000 won and wheels the bent bicycle away. The crumpled bills and bent wheel are what remain.

choices.text: Get angry — 'You need to watch where you're driving.'
choices.result_text:
The words he has been holding back come out. She bows her head.
'...I'm really sorry.'

It seems genuine. That makes it impossible to keep shouting.
{name} sighs and wheels the bent bicycle away.
The weight of her gaze lingers.

description_orthodox:
At dusk in spring rain, on a back road in Sinchon. {name} is riding a secondhand bicycle to save on transit fares.

A black sedan comes around the corner and clips the front wheel. {name} falls onto the rain-slick road. His knee bleeds, and the front wheel bends.

The car door opens. A woman who looks to be in her early thirties steps out into the rain, visibly shaken.
"You should really see a doctor—"

{name} tallies the wheel repair, the time a hospital visit would take, and the work still left today. He cannot afford to spend much longer in the road.
description_unorthodox:
One rainy spring evening, on a back road in Sinchon. {name} is riding a secondhand bicycle to save on transit fares.

A black sedan comes around the corner and clips the front wheel. The impact sends {name} down onto the rain-slick road.

Getting up, {name} catches the plate. A foreign car. A woman who looks to be in her early thirties steps out and looks between his knee and the bicycle.

"You should really see a doctor—"

{name} checks the hours left in the day and the bent front wheel. She has caused the collision; now he has to decide what to ask for.

title: You Again
description:
Late at night, at a bus stop near Sinchon Station. The rain has just let up.

A black sedan eases to the edge of the wet road. The driver's door opens and a woman steps out.

It is the driver who hit the bicycle.

She recognizes {name} too. Her eyes widen.
"...Wait. You're the one from that day, aren't you?"

The arrival time changes on the bus display. This time there is no counter, and no one else between them.

description_memory_if_known.bicycle_repaired_with_jiyeon_cash: The day after the crash, {name} spent all 80,000 won on the repair. The new front wheel no longer pulled to one side.
description_memory_if_known.bicycle_repaired_after_delay: {name} put off the repair for a while, but eventually used the 80,000 won from the crash to replace the front wheel.
description_memory_if_known.bicycle_left_unrepaired: The bicycle with the bent wheel was still parked outside the goshiwon. That day too, {name} tapped a transit card and came to this bus stop.
description_memory_if_known.bicycle_wheel_bent: The bicycle's front wheel had stayed bent since the crash. There had been no way to contact the driver again.

choices.text: Pretend not to recognize her and watch the bus display
choices.result_text:
{name} keeps his eyes on the display.

The woman takes one step closer first.
"Excuse me. Is the bicycle all right? I've been worrying about it since that day."

Only then does {name} turn. An awkward silence passes.
"I'm Han Jiyeon. I thought I should at least tell you my name."

Bus headlights spread across the wet road in the distance.

choices.text: "You were driving that day, right?" Speak first
choices.result_text:
The tension leaves her face.
"You remember. I've been worrying about what happened that day."
"There was no need to go looking for me."
"Still, I told myself I'd introduce myself properly if I saw you again."

She hesitates, then holds out a hand.
"I'm Han Jiyeon. I wanted you to know my name this time."

For the first time, there is a name between them.

title: Let Me Make It Up to You
description:
A few days later, on a main road in the same neighborhood. Rain was falling again.

The black sedan stopped beside the bus shelter. Han Jiyeon got out with an umbrella. This was not another chance encounter.

"Just let me buy you one coffee. If not that, then a meal. It's been weighing on me. That day was my fault, and you walked away without taking anything."

For days, a message about his father's medication and job alerts had been piling up on the same phone screen. Now Jiyeon wanted to repay a debt of conscience.

She seemed sincere. But if one coffee became a beginning, the distance between their worlds would come into sharper focus.

choices.text: Decline — "Don't worry about it. I'm really fine."
choices.result_text:
{name} shakes his head and walks toward the subway station.

Jiyeon doesn't follow. Instead, she calls out behind him.
"Why do you keep running away?"

{name} doesn't stop. But the words keep following him.
— Running? Is this running away?
That day, Jiyeon grew more curious about the person called {name}.

choices.text: Accept the coffee — just once
choices.result_text:
They sat across from each other at a cafe. She had a 6,500 won latte; {name}, the cheapest americano.

Jiyeon talked a lot. About studying abroad, her father's company, her stifling family.
{name} mostly just listened.

"And you? What do you do?"
"...A bit of this and that."
She didn't press further. She just smiled.
"Let's meet again. Next time you're buying, not me."
As if there would be a next time.

choices.text: Be honest — "The worlds we live in are too different."
choices.result_text:
For the first time, {name} spoke honestly.
"Do you know how many months of my rent your car is worth? Buying one coffee is nothing to you, but to me it isn't."

Jiyeon was quiet for a while.
"...So that's why you just left that day?"
"Yes."
"But you know what." She looked {name} straight in the eye.
"I've never met someone like that. Which makes me want to know you more."
That look shook {name}.

title: Her World
description:
A few days later, Jiyeon contacted {name} again. This time, she asked him to join her for lunch.

She took {name} to a Korean restaurant in Cheongdam. Lunch set: 40,000 won.

{name} opened the menu, closed it, opened it again, closed it.

She pretended not to notice. Or really didn't.
After ordering she said:

"I'm interested in investing, actually. I've been studying because of my father's company, but no one around me is into this stuff. It gets frustrating."

{name} thought for a moment.
What exactly did this person want? It was impossible to tell.

choices.text: 'I'm studying it too. Let's talk.' — Approach as investment partners.
choices.result_text:
Two hours of real estate, pre-sales, investment talk.
Jiyeon knew a lot. Had studied hard.
What {name} knew and what she knew were different. Because of where they came from.
{name} tried to pay for the lunch. Reached — but she'd already put down the card.

choices.text: 'Let's just enjoy lunch today.' — Don't define the relationship yet.
choices.result_text:
Lunch was good. Conversation light.
On the way out she said: 'Where do you want to go next time?'
'Next time' was created. What kind of next time — still unknown.

title: After
description:
The morning after {name} told her everything —
Jiyeon sent a message first.

'I'm scared you might still be angry, oppa.
I said so much yesterday... I'm kind of strange, aren't I?'

{name} stared at the phone.

A woman with three layers of reason.
Because of her father's company. Because she needed an investor. And because she wanted someone close.

What can this become?

choices.text: 'You're not weird. That's just being human.' — Accept it.
choices.result_text:
Sent the reply.
A moment later, hers: 'You're strange too, oppa. That's why I like you.'
{name} half-smiled. Felt like there was one more reason to reach Gangnam.

choices.text: 'Jiyeon — Gangnam still comes first for me.' — Draw a clear line.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon went quiet, then: '...you understand. That's more honest.'
The next day, a document on pre-sale rights came from her.
'If you need help on this side, reach out. That part was genuine.'
Business partners — without the feelings.

choices.text: 'I understand all three reasons.' — No judgment.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon went quiet a moment, then said: '...That's the scariest thing you've said. Because you're grateful.'
Gangnam and feelings and calculation all tangled in this.
Decided not to give up on it for being complicated.

title: Ten Years
description:
One KakaoTalk message.
"Hey {name}! It's Jaehyuk. Choi Jaehyuk from the army. Remember? I'm in Seoul — let's grab a drink."

Profile picture: him in front of a foreign car.
22 years old. Same barracks. Inseparable through our whole service, then nothing after discharge.

The Jaehyuk at the pojangmacha was different.
Good clothes. Expensive watch. Confidence in every word.
"You haven't changed at all! Let's drink."

choices.text: Glad to see him — an old friend after a long time.
choices.result_text:
Old army stories stretched into the night.
First time laughing out loud in a while. A welcome face in a hard stretch.
'Let's meet up often, {name}. You'll be in touch.'
Jaehyuk seemed genuine. At least that night.

choices.text: Glad, but keeping some distance.
choices.result_text:
Clinked glasses and smiled — but something sat uneasily.
Someone who contacts you after ten years is doing this well.
Why now, why you.
{name} pushed that thought away. It's an old friend.

description_orthodox:
KakaoTalk. Choi Jaehyuk. Army.

Ten years.

The Jaehyuk at the pojangmacha used a foreign car as his profile photo.
Good clothes. Expensive watch. The kind of confidence that fills a room.

{name} smiled warmly and quietly calculated.
What had this person been doing for ten years since discharge.
Why this call, why now.
description_unorthodox:
KakaoTalk. Jaehyuk. Ten years.

Foreign car profile. Expensive watch. Paid for three rounds at the pojangmacha.

Maybe he's just a military buddy who did well.
Or maybe he wants something.

{name} accepted the drink. Too early to tell.

title: Brothers
description:
After that, Jaehyuk kept in touch.
Bought meals, bought drinks, sometimes tried to slip money over.

'You're struggling lately, aren't you? Take this, come on, we're not strangers.'
{name} didn't take it. But the gesture felt genuine.

Today: a café. Jaehyuk takes out his phone.
'{name}, honestly I've been making pretty good money investing. Pretty good money.'
Shows the screen. Profit graph. Numbers going sharply up.
'If you're interested I'll fill you in. No pressure.'

choices.text: Show interest — 'How does it work?'
choices.result_text:
Jaehyuk's eyes lit up.
'I knew you'd get it. I'll tell you everything slowly.'
The returns he showed were unrealistically good.
Too good to be good — {name} forgot that then.

choices.text: Thanks, but pass — 'Investing isn't really my thing.'
choices.result_text:
'Ah, I'm not saying do it now. Just saying.'
Jaehyuk laughed and changed subjects.
But that profit graph stayed in the mind.
If it's real... {name} shook the thought off. For now.

choices.text: Those returns are too good — quietly start to wonder.
choices.result_text:
'Jaehyuk — this looks too good. Is this actually real?'
Jaehyuk's expression froze for half a second, then cleared.
'Ha, that's exactly why everyone doubts it and passes. Your call.'
That half-second — {name} didn't miss it.

title: The Offer
description:
Jaehyuk called a meeting. Hotel lounge.

"I'll be straight with you. {name}, this is just for you.
Something big came in. Triple the principal. But the window closes this week."

He leans forward. Voice drops.

"You want Gangnam, right? How long will that take on a salary? At our age, there's no answer in a paycheck.
You trust me, right? We lived and died together in there."

Triple the principal. This week only.
Both sentences landed at the same time.

choices.text: Send the 3 million won Jaehyuk asked for.
choices.result_text:
He sent the 3 million won Jaehyuk had asked for.
Jaehyuk patted his shoulder. "Good call. You'll be smiling soon."

That night, {name} couldn't sleep.
The amount he had just sent kept looking larger than everything left in the account.

choices.text: Put in a portion — want in, but won't bet it all.
choices.result_text:
'Jaehyuk, this much is all I can do. More would be too much.'
Jaehyuk looks faintly disappointed. 'Well... still something. Thanks.'
Not going all-in was an instinct.
That instinct might save {name} later.

choices.text: Refuse. And quietly start looking into it.
choices.result_text:
'Let me think about it.' {name} left.
Went home and started searching.
The investment product Jaehyuk mentioned. The company name. Similar fraud cases.

Results started appearing one by one.
A cold feeling ran down the spine.

description_orthodox:
Hotel lounge. Jaehyuk's expression turned serious.

Triple the principal. This week only.

{name} analyzed the structure of those two sentences.
If 'triple' is the hook, 'this week only' is the device that kills thinking time.
Textbook pattern.

Jaehyuk said: "We lived and died together in there."

Because that sentence was true — knowing he should be more careful — {name} wavered anyway.
description_unorthodox:
Hotel lounge. Jaehyuk leaned across the table.

'Triple the principal.'

Every approach {name} had tried — stocks, investment, racetrack — none of them came close to that number.

'This week only.'

The pressure feeling. Not sure if Jaehyuk created it or {name} did.
"We lived and died together in there."

That line was the trigger.

title: No Answer
description:
On settlement day, the only thing growing in Jaehyuk's chat was the row of question marks {name} had sent. No Read receipt appeared. Calls rang out and disconnected; the profile photo and status line vanished.

On the third night, {name} searched the company name. The first result was an investment-fraud victims' forum. A pinned post said, "Do not delete contracts or transfer records." Beneath it was the name being reported: Choi Jaehyuk.

{name} took out the application copy from the hotel lounge. His own signature was on the last page, Jaehyuk's name in the introducer box. He opened the old PDF of Father's guarantee from the bottom of the drawer. Different documents, but the same rectangular space where someone who trusted another person surrendered his name.

A forum message arrived: "If it's the same man, send the records first." What {name} wanted to ask Jaehyuk and the time already lost by strangers now occupied the same screen.

choices.text: Preserve the application and read the victims' posts first — postpone Jaehyuk's explanation
choices.result_text: {name} muted Jaehyuk's chat and renamed both PDFs by date. He opened the first victim's post. The join date and amount were different. The opening sentence was disturbingly familiar.

choices.text: Leave Jaehyuk one last voice message — postpone checking the records
choices.result_text: {name} pressed Call again. After the ringing came the recording prompt. "Jaehyuk. Forget the money. Tell me yourself what you put in front of me that night." He stayed on the line until the message sent.

description_if_known.felt_jaehyuk_kindness:
On settlement day, the only thing growing in Jaehyuk's chat was the row of question marks {name} had sent. No Read receipt appeared. Calls rang out and disconnected; the profile photo and status line vanished.

On the third night, a search for the company brought up an investment-fraud victims' forum. The reported name was Choi Jaehyuk. A pinned post warned visitors not to delete contracts or transfer records.

{name} opened the hotel application beside the old PDF of Father's guarantee. His signature, Jaehyuk's name, and Father's faded signature sat inside nearly identical boxes. Then he remembered Jaehyuk offering the HR manager's card. "We're not strangers, are we?"

Calling every kindness part of the scheme would make anger easy. Believing the kindness was real would make closing the screen easy. With neither answer proven, the victims' message and Jaehyuk's empty chat remained lit together.
description_if_known.asked_partial_return:
On settlement day, the only thing growing in Jaehyuk's chat was the row of question marks {name} had sent. No Read receipt appeared. Calls rang out and disconnected; the profile photo vanished.

On the third night, a search for the company brought up an investment-fraud victims' forum. The reported name was Choi Jaehyuk. A pinned post warned visitors not to delete contracts or transfer records.

The day {name} asked for even part of his money back, Jaehyuk looked away for a beat and smiled. "Next month. I mean it." {name} believed him and put the application copy in a drawer. Now its last page showed his own signature and Jaehyuk's name. Beside it, Father's old guarantee held the same kind of space for the person who would carry the responsibility.

A forum message arrived: "If it's the same man, send the records first." {name} had to choose between waiting one more month and reading the words of people who already had.

title: The Same Sentence
description:
The first post read, "We went to high school together. I trusted him."

The second began with an army photo. "He said we had lived and died together."

A third victim had uploaded a profit screenshot. "He said he had put in his own money first." The dates and numbers differed; the layout matched the one Jaehyuk had shown {name}.

Classmate, senior, friend of a cousin. Only the relationship changed. He presented closeness as proof, and people collateralized their own memories.

choices.text: Read every account the other victims left behind.
choices.result_text: By the last page, daylight had reached the window. Before counting the money, {name} counted the people who had believed the same sentence.

title: After the Ringing
description:
An automated voice answered. "The person you are calling is unavailable. You will be connected to voicemail."

After the beep, {name} still could not speak. He swallowed once. "Jaehyuk. Forget the money. Tell me yourself. Was everything you said at that lounge a lie too?"

The moment he sent it, a notification appeared from the victims' forum. A stranger had written, "You were army buddies? I served in the same unit with him too."

Jaehyuk did not answer. Instead, one more person appeared who said he knew him.

choices.text: Close the silent chat and organize the evidence.
choices.result_text: The voice message remained marked Sent. It never gained a Read receipt. {name} placed the call log, transfer history, and victims' posts side by side.

title: The Empty Place
description:
Two in the morning. No answer came.

Instead of Jaehyuk, the screen kept filling with posts from the people he had passed through. {name} was one of them now.

The photograph of them laughing and the bank transfer lived on the same phone. The loss was already decided. What remained was deciding who {name} would be after it.

choices.text: Stay in bed for the next few days.
choices.result_text:
For days, {name} stayed in bed and stared at the ceiling. The account was empty. Gangnam felt farther away.

But at rock bottom, there was nowhere lower to go. Getting back up was the only thing left. Someday, no matter what, he would get that money back.

choices.text: Join the forum and post: 'He scammed me too.'
choices.result_text:
{name} joined the forum and posted.
'He scammed me too. We were army buddies.'

Replies appeared. 'Same here.' 'He was my classmate.'
He always targeted someone close and used trust as a weapon.

The victims began to gather, with {name} near the center. Getting something back might not be impossible.

choices.text: (The photo from that night came to mind.)
choices.result_text: {name} opened the phone gallery. One photograph of the two of them outside the pojangmacha was still there. He looked for a long time at the one he had never deleted.

title: Counter
description:
{name} spent a month quietly gathering.
Jaehyuk's investment product structure. Money flow. Testimony from other victims.

It was a textbook Ponzi scheme. New money covering old payouts.
Once the structure was understood, the weak points appeared.

Met Jaehyuk again. This time {name} called the meeting.
'Jaehyuk. I know everything. The company structure. The victims.'
Jaehyuk's face goes white.
'...What are you going to do.'

A moment of decision. What kind of person will {name} become?

choices.text: Turn him in — do the right thing.
choices.result_text:
Handed the evidence to the police. Along with victim statements.
Jaehyuk was arrested. {name} didn't get the money back.
But at least stopped more people from being hurt.

Im Sangchul said: 'Good. You protected something more important than money.'
{name} had empty hands — but could look in the mirror.

choices.text: Hold the leverage and negotiate — get my money back, and then some.
choices.result_text:
'you won't report you. But give you triple your money back. One week.'
Jaehyuk nodded, trembling. The money came.

One step closer to Gangnam. But that night,
{name} spent a long time thinking about how they were any different from Jaehyuk.
Couldn't find an answer.

choices.text: Pull him in and run a bigger scheme — turn fraud into business.
choices.result_text:
'Instead of reporting — let's work together. But this time, properly.'
In Jaehyuk's eyes: relief and fear mixed.

{name} crossed the line. Gangnam will get closer.
Fast. Dirty.
Is the apartment Dad never got — supposed to be bought with this money?
That question, {name} decided not to ask. For now.

title: Sangchul's Call
description:
A call from Im Sangchul after a long time.

'Minjun, I heard you've saved up some seed money. Something just came up.'

A villa right before redevelopment. The owner in a rush, listed well below market.
Sangchul had held it through his contacts.

'If the redevelopment is confirmed within a year, you're looking at double. If not — it sits.
Thirty years in this business, I think this one has decent odds.
But it's your call. I'm not recommending or warning.'

A significant portion of current funds. Not a gamble — but not safe either.

choices.text: Trust him — trust Sangchul's thirty years.
choices.result_text:
Stamped the contract with Sangchul.
He pats the shoulder. 'Good. Now waiting is the work.'
Real estate is different from stocks. Slower — but heavier.
Whatever happens, {name} got on the board for the first time.

choices.text: Put in only a little — don't get greedy.
choices.result_text:
'Not overextending is right.' Sangchul nods.
Half confidence, half bet.
{name} decided to stake only what fits in the bucket. That's how you last.

choices.text: Pass — protect the money for now.
choices.result_text:
'Good. The times you don't act are what keep you alive.'
Sangchul wasn't disappointed.
But a few months later, the redevelopment news came out.
Sangchul didn't mention it. {name} noticed on their own.

title: Make the Seed Money Work
description:
About two weeks after their first meeting, {name} returned to the Sinchon real-estate office. Im Sangchul held out a cup of tea.

"You thinking about investing?"

Before answering, {name} looked at the man's hands. Hands that had worked.
Manual labor, night-guard shifts, real-estate gigs. Two buildings now.

"I am — but I don't know anything yet."

"That's the most honest answer there is." Im Sangchul smiled.
"Someone who knows nothing is the easiest to teach. It's the ones who pretend to know that are the problem."

choices.text: "How should I start?" — ask in earnest
choices.result_text:
Sangchul thought for a long while before speaking.
"Start small at first. With money you can afford to lose and still learn from.
You lose some, and the market starts coming into focus."

After leaving the office, {name} opened the investment tab for the first time.
choices.bridge_summary: He followed Sangchul's advice: enter the market only with enough to lose and learn from.

choices.text: "Shouldn't saving come first?"
choices.result_text:
"Saving's the foundation, sure. But saving alone will never get you there."
Sangchul said it with a smile.
"Anyway, give it some thought. There's no rush."
{name} left the office. Something sat heavy in a corner of his chest.
choices.bridge_summary: Sangchul's warning that saving alone would never be enough stayed behind every calculation that week.

choices.text: "I have my own way of doing things."
choices.result_text:
"Sure. You've got to figure it out for yourself in the end."
Sangchul laughed, unbothered.
{name} left the office and opened the notebook. He wrote 'My way,' then stopped.
The pen left one dark dot beneath the empty line.
choices.bridge_summary: After rejecting Sangchul's method, he wrote 'My way' in the notebook and left the line beneath it empty.

description_orthodox:
About two weeks after their first meeting, {name} returned to the Sinchon real-estate office. Im Sangchul held out a cup of tea.

"You thinking about investing?"

{name} left the cup where it was and looked first at the business card beside the handle. Its corners were worn. Three numbers had been written on the back in ballpoint pen.

"I am — but I don't know yet."

"That's the most honest answer there is." Im Sangchul smiled.
He did not pull the untouched cup back toward himself.
description_unorthodox:
About two weeks after their first meeting, {name} returned to the Sinchon real-estate office. Im Sangchul held out a cup of tea.

"You thinking about investing?"

"Sure." {name} answered right away.

"Why?"

That stung. Why. Too simple to call it the money; too long to explain if it was Gangnam.

"I haven't sorted it out yet."

"Let me know when you do." Im Sangchul smiled.

title: The Presale Right
description:
Jiyeon called him aside, quietly.

"My father's company is putting up a presale development in Gangnam. It hasn't gone public yet.
If you just put down the deposit, the premium will be enormous. I'm only telling you, oppa."

{name} hesitated. This was an opportunity Jiyeon's world was offering him.
Take it, and he'd close in on Gangnam. But in that same moment, he'd be in her debt.
He'd be setting one foot inside her world.

"Why are you giving this to me?"
"...You really have to ask?" She smiled.

Money and feelings, both on the line.

choices.text: Take the chance — to get closer to Gangnam
choices.result_text:
He put down the deposit. He'd stepped one foot into Jiyeon's world.

She smiled, satisfied. "Good call."
But {name} knew. This wasn't free.
The closer Gangnam got, the closer she got too. Like a debt.

choices.text: Turn it down — I want to get there under my own power
choices.result_text:
"Thank you. But I want to do this on my own."
Jiyeon's expression hardened, subtly.
"...You really are a strange one, oppa. You're turning this down?"

She didn't understand. But {name} —
he liked the version of himself that owed her nothing.
Gangnam slipped further away, but he could hold his head up.

title: Easy Money
description:
The goshiwon, 2 a.m. At the top of the phone was a text canceling this week's overnight loading shift. On the desk lay a reminder for next week's 650,000-won rent transfer. One look at the balance brought the sigh first.{v2_month_one_episode_echo}

An unknown number texted.
"Lend us your bankbook and debit card. Two million on the spot. You do nothing. One month, zero risk."

When {name} did not answer, another line arrived.
"Decide tonight and you'll have it within an hour. Delete this chat."

He knew the job: a mule account. Doing nothing meant lending out his name and account while other people's money moved through it.

Two million won would cover three months of rent and the overdue utilities. Beneath the rent reminder, the final receipt from Father's debt repayment still showed at the edge. The cursor blinked in the reply box.

choices.text: Block the number — accept the rent bill and tomorrow's labor
choices.result_text:
The chat vanished when {name} tapped Block. The two million won did not arrive, and rent day did not move.

He called the foreman who had canceled the shift. "If a spot opens tomorrow morning, call me." After a pause, the foreman told him to be there at 4:20.

With the phone facedown, the repayment receipt and rent reminder came back into view. {name} set the alarm for 4:20 a.m.

choices.text: Hand over the bankbook, card, and PIN — take 2,000,000 won tonight
choices.result_text:
His reply brought a subway-locker number. {name} sealed the bankbook and debit card in an envelope and sent the PIN. The answer came at once: "Do not open the account from now on."

An hour later, two million won in cash waited in the same locker. Back in the room, {name} circled the rent reminder. He entered the amount in his notebook, then stopped with the pen at the source column.

title: The Place It Passed Through

choices.text: Check the signed-in devices and transfer limit again, then take the remaining night shifts
choices.result_text:
{name} changed his password and lowered the daily transfer limit. The device list showed only the phone in his hand, and the recruiter's number was still sitting at the bottom of the block list.

When he called the foreman, only the Thursday and Saturday predawn slots remained that week. {name} took both. After the call, he wrote the new shift times beside the rent reminder. The two million won he had refused had become two more mornings of labor and a balance that was still short.

description:
Several weeks after refusing the first offer, {name} came back to his room from a 4:20 a.m. loading shift. When he took off his gloves, the blister in his palm had split. His banking app showed the rent transfer due in three days and, first of all, the balance it could not cover. He opened the security alert and checked the signed-in devices. His own phone was the only one listed.

A news chyron reported the arrest of a mule-account recruitment ring. {name} scrolled all the way down his block list to make sure that number was still there. Keeping his account had not paid the rent for him. The two million won had never arrived. What remained were two open night shifts that week and a transfer limit he needed to reset. Then the foreman texted: 'Another spot opened tonight.'

title: A Return Request on the Account He Lent Out
description:
Some time later, out in the rain, the bank's fraud-response team called. The employee read out the times when thirty million won had entered and left the account in {name}'s name, then asked by the end of the day whether he would consent to return an initial 1.5 million won through the victim-funds process. Consent required his ID and a visit to a branch. The account was already frozen.

The date of the two-million-won payment he had first received and the time of the return request now sat together in the call record. Before the call had ended, a text from a different number covered the top of the screen.

"Clean work. Bring three more accounts, one million each. Your name is already on the list anyway."

The bank asked when he could authorize the return. The recruiter sent a subway-locker number. Both records stayed on the same screen.

choices.text: Go to the branch, sign the 1.5-million-won return authorization, and close the account and numbers
choices.result_text:
{name} handed his rain-soaked ID across the counter and signed the authorization to return 1.5 million won. While the teller stamped it received, he blocked each number the recruiter had used and filed to close the account he had lent out.

The receipt recorded his consent to return 1.5 million won and noted that further verification remained. His wallet held the closure receipt and the case officer's card. Outside the bank, the recruiter's last locker number was still visible in the blocked-notification log.

choices.text: Refuse the return request and put three bankbook-and-card sets in the locker
choices.result_text:
{name} told the bank employee he would not consent, then texted the recruiter: "I can get three." Three days later, he put three sets of bankbooks and debit cards bearing other people's names into a subway locker and sent the three PINs.

An hour later, an envelope holding three million won in cash waited in the same compartment. As {name} took it out, another name and account number arrived on his phone. The banking app retained the rejected-return record; his inbox retained the next locker address.

title: Twenty Minutes Beyond Compensation
description:
Even after the accident settlement was over, Han Jiyeon's name remained in {name}'s chat list. He rewrote the message three times to keep compensation and the bicycle out of it, then contacted her first. 'This has nothing to do with what happened before. I would like to see you again briefly. I will wait across from that street at seven on Friday.'

Her reply came fifteen minutes later. 'I can spare twenty minutes.' The standby list for the weekend loading shift {name} could have taken at that hour filled without him. On Friday, the black sedan stopped across the road, and Jiyeon crossed alone. She checked her watch once and folded her umbrella.

"If this isn't about compensation, I want to hear why you asked to see me again. Within twenty minutes."

choices.text: "I contacted you because I was curious about Han Jiyeon, not about that day."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon did not smile right away. Instead, they stepped into a small café across the road. She set a timer on her phone, placed it on the table, and asked first about {name}'s work and why he had come to Seoul. Her questions were short, but she did not let gaps in his answers pass.

When the twenty-minute alarm sounded, she turned it off and stood. "This time is open next Friday too. Then you can ask the questions." The date went into the calendar. The closed loading-shift list stayed closed.

choices.text: "Instead of sitting in the car, would you walk one block with me?"
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon glanced back at the sedan across the road, then opened her umbrella again. "One block." They avoided the alley where the accident had happened and walked along the main road. She said her driver had the day off and she had driven herself. {name} said he still had not repaired the bicycle.

At the end of the block, Jiyeon stopped. "Next Friday, let's sit down and talk. Same time, at a café nearby." After she returned to the car, one exact date remained beneath the empty umbrella.

choices.text: "I'm sorry I asked so late. Let me buy dinner next Friday."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon's gaze moved once between {name}'s worn cuff and the restaurant sign across the street. "If you're turning accident money into dinner money, I'm not coming."

"That isn't what I mean."

After a silence, she opened her own calendar. "Then we pay separately. Next Friday at seven." She sent him a location. On {name}'s screen, the closed work roster and the first dinner appointment he had set sat one above the other.

title: The First Check
description:
On Friday evening, {name} reached the small restaurant he and Jiyeon had chosen before seven. Jiyeon also arrived alone on time and chose a table inside rather than by the window. After they ordered, a late alert surfaced on his phone: 'Work documents due 6:30 p.m.' A reply beneath it said this round would accept nothing unless he had appeared at the counter by that time.

Jiyeon did not ask what the alert said. She pushed the water glass toward {name}, then looked once from his eyes moving over the menu prices to the phone that would not go dark. She folded her napkin into a precise rectangle.

"Don't explain what you gave up to come here. I want to talk to the person who came today. Just don't leave your mind somewhere else while you sit here." The first plate arrived. The closed counter's timestamp remained on the screen.

choices.text: Turn the phone facedown and ask first about Jiyeon's ordinary day
choices.result_text:
When {name} asked, "How did you spend today?" Jiyeon stopped her chopsticks as if the question had surprised her. Instead of naming her company or family, she talked about a proposal rejected that morning and the lunch she had skipped. {name} told her about a torn glove at the loading dock.

When the check came, they each paid their exact share. Outside, Jiyeon said, "That was a decent question tonight," and walked toward the car first. The reply from the closed work counter still waited on the facedown phone.

choices.text: "The truth is, I missed a 6:30 deadline. I still chose to come tonight."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon did not offer comfort first. "Don't say you missed it because of me. {name} is the one who decided to come." Her voice was cool, but she did not leave. She asked why both the deadline and this promise had been pushed to the same day.

{name} explained the shape of his week without making an excuse. At the register, Jiyeon paid only her share. "Next time, don't offer what you missed as though it were a gift." Her words outside were composed. Only two empty plates remained at the table.

choices.text: "I will leave at nine. I want to set the boundary I can actually keep tonight."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon checked her watch. "Setting the time before a meeting isn't bad. At least it means you won't vanish." They agreed to ask only one thing each before then. Jiyeon asked what {name} was truly looking at whenever he said Gangnam.

At nine, {name} set the check between them and paid his share first. Jiyeon paid her share at once. They parted at the exact time they had named, each carrying one question that had not been asked.

title: The Answer Left Waiting
description:
After their last meeting, the conversation with Jiyeon had stopped at one message {name} never answered. Several weeks later, on a Saturday in the ninth month, he contacted her first. 'I want to answer properly for what I brushed aside then. May I tell you in person?'

Jiyeon replied, 'If you know what it was you postponed,' and sent the address of a small café she chose. She sat in front of an empty glass she had not ordered. When {name} arrived, she pointed to the chair across from her instead of commenting on the delay. At that hour, other chats still held half-written lines and records of answers he had postponed, each with its own time.

"I didn't come just to hear a pleasant answer. I came to see whether the person who showed up late knows what he made wait." Jiyeon did not look away.

choices.text: "Even without the accident, I would have been curious about Han Jiyeon."
choices.result_text:
For a while, Jiyeon only touched the rim of the glass. "That would have been easier to hear that day." Then she ordered coffee for the first time. {name} explained why he had been curious, and she named what had frustrated her, one sentence at a time.

Outside the café, Jiyeon did not set the next appointment first. She only said, "Don't make me wait for your reply this time." Beneath the finished conversation with her, other chat records where he had postponed an answer remained in {name}'s chat list.

choices.text: "It is also true that I was curious about the world you live in. I wanted to hide that."
choices.result_text:

title: The Workplace After the Drinks

title: The Address and the Introducer

title: The Second Coffee
description:
Out checking studio-apartment listings, he passed through that neighborhood and the light on at Sangchul's office caught his eye.

The story of coming up to Seoul from Chungcheong without a single connection.

Sitting across from her at the café, {name} already remembered what Sangchul had said.
'That woman needs presale numbers — she's after your money.'

She opened her mouth.
The story of her father's company. The presale targets. And why she'd pitched it to Minjun.

"But that's not all of it.
My wish for you to do well was real too.
And... I was curious about you, and I wanted to be near you."

"All three are tangled together, and I don't know what kind of person I am.
Am I a bad person?"

{name} already knew. Which made it stranger still: complication came before anger.

choices.result_text:
"...You knew?"

That silence was the answer.
